skill.name: brewpage-publish-safe
skill.description: Publish approved HTML, Markdown, JSON, files, and static sites to BrewPage. Reuse locally stored anonymous owner credentials to update the exact saved publication.
skill.summary: Publish content to BrewPage and update the exact saved item from the same workspace.
skill.author: kochetkov-ma

security_audit.summary: Most alerts match documented BrewPage requests, private state operations, fixed utility calls, or literal text. No evidence of deliberate credential exfiltration or reviewer-directed prompt injection was found. Residual risks include non-isolated Python startup, inherited environment settings, and incomplete validation of publication inputs and results.

remediation.issue: Some publish-time Python helpers are not isolated.
remediation.suggestion: Use isolated Python with site initialization disabled for every helper. Resolve tool binaries from a trusted environment.

remediation.issue: Child utilities inherit environment settings that are not needed.
remediation.suggestion: Pass a minimal explicit child environment. Clear Git repository-discovery overrides before checking the state path.

remediation.issue: Archive review text mixes untrusted names and runner status.
remediation.suggestion: Escape filenames in display output and encode the entry and decision in structured data. Keep the digest tied to the actual upload snapshot.

remediation.issue: Reserved-name filtering does not prevent accidental disclosure of embedded secrets.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose the limits of filename checks. Scan publication inputs for secrets and reject opaque nested archives unless they are separately reviewed.

remediation.issue: Password file checks do not protect the later copy from path replacement.
remediation.suggestion: Open the source once without following symlinks. Verify the opened descriptor and derive the private header from those same bytes.

remediation.issue: The reader link can use a host not bound to the confirmed publication.
remediation.suggestion: Require a supported BrewPage host and matching publication route, or verify an authorized custom host using trusted service metadata before reporting it.

semantic_findings.title: Python Startup Is Not Consistently Isolated
semantic_findings.description: Some publish-time helpers start Python without isolated mode. Local module lookup and interpreter startup can execute code outside the installed skill before content validation completes.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The HTML, UTF-8, and digest helpers omit the interpreter flags used for history and snapshot operations. The runner does not establish a trusted working directory.

semantic_findings.title: Archive Review Includes Untrusted Filename Text
semantic_findings.description: Skipped filenames can enter the review transcript without escaping. The runner also derives the entry point from printed text instead of a separate structured field.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Names with line breaks can enter the skipped list, which the formatter prints verbatim. The shell later reads an entry value from that same manifest output.

semantic_findings.title: Credential Filtering Does Not Inspect File Contents
semantic_findings.description: The skill relies on names, file metadata, and known path identities to screen uploads. An approved file can still contain exposed secrets, including inside nested archives.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code checks reserved names and selected file identities, not arbitrary payload content. The runner sends selected content to BrewPage after those checks.

semantic_findings.title: Password Source Validation Is Not Bound to the Read
semantic_findings.description: The runner checks the selected password file and later reopens its path. A local replacement can change the password or place unintended data in the publication header.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The copy uses the path again without retaining the validated descriptor. The later check validates password syntax, not the identity of the source file.

semantic_findings.title: Reader Links Are Not Bound to an Approved Host
semantic_findings.description: The receipt checks the official write endpoint but can display an arbitrary HTTPS reader host as confirmed. That can mislead users about where a publication is hosted.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The reader identity check applies only to the main BrewPage hostname. The runner displays the validated string without requesting it or checking another host binding.

medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: The Git safety check inherits repository-discovery overrides from the caller. These can invalidate the check that credential state is outside a Git working tree.

medium_findings.title: Archive Review Includes Untrusted Filename Text
medium_findings.description: Skipped filenames can enter the review transcript without escaping. The runner also derives the entry point from printed text instead of a separate structured field.
medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: Names with line breaks can enter the skipped list, which the formatter prints verbatim. The shell later reads an entry value from that same manifest output.

medium_findings.title: Credential Filtering Does Not Inspect File Contents
medium_findings.description: The skill relies on names, file metadata, and known path identities to screen uploads. An approved file can still contain exposed secrets, including inside nested archives.
medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code checks reserved names and selected file identities, not arbitrary payload content. The runner sends selected content to BrewPage after those checks.

medium_findings.title: Password Source Validation Is Not Bound to the Read
medium_findings.description: The runner checks the selected password file and later reopens its path. A local replacement can change the password or place unintended data in the publication header.
medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: The copy uses the path again without retaining the validated descriptor. The later check validates password syntax, not the identity of the source file.

medium_findings.title: Reader Links Are Not Bound to an Approved Host
medium_findings.description: The receipt checks the official write endpoint but can display an arbitrary HTTPS reader host as confirmed. That can mislead users about where a publication is hosted.
medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: The reader identity check applies only to the main BrewPage hostname. The runner displays the validated string without requesting it or checking another host binding.

low_findings.title: Environment variable object
low_findings.confidence_reasoning: ZIP utilities inherit the caller environment after only ZIP option defaults are removed. This unnecessarily exposes unrelated environment values to child processes.

content.user_title: Publish and Update Content on BrewPage
content.value_statement: Publishing a file or site can leave you without a clear way to find and update it later. This skill checks site archives and stores anonymous ownership records for later updates.
actual_capabilities: Publish explicitly approved HTML, Markdown, JSON, or individual files to the BrewPage API.
Build a ZIP from a selected site directory or inspect an existing site ZIP and report its member list, size, and entry point.
Pause flagged site uploads for approval tied to the reviewed archive digest.
Store anonymous owner credentials and management links in private, workspace-specific application state.
Update the exact saved publication without changing its expiry or access choices.
Report pending create attempts and recover saved owner receipts from the original workspace.
limitations: Publishing requires network access to BrewPage. Local probes do not upload content.
The documented setup uses macOS or Linux with Bash, Python, Node.js, curl, and jq. Site workflows also require ZIP tools.
This edition does not support connected account ownership or private receipt delivery.
Archive checks are not a full secret scan. Review file contents before authorizing publication.

use_cases.title: Share Release Notes
use_cases.description: Publish approved Markdown with link-only access, then update the same page using its saved reader link.

use_cases.title: Review a Static Site Bundle
use_cases.description: Check which files a site archive contains and approve flagged entries only after comparing the manifest with the intended release.

use_cases.title: Resolve an Uncertain Publication
use_cases.description: Check a pending create and recover saved owner proof before deciding whether another publication is needed.

prompt_templates.title: Check a File Locally
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: inspect selected content without publishing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Probe [file path] locally and report its detected type and size. Do not contact BrewPage.

prompt_templates.title: Publish Approved Notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Publish [Markdown file] to BrewPage in namespace [namespace] for seven days. Use link-only access without a password. Report the reader link and owner storage status.

prompt_templates.title: Publish a Reviewed Site
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: publish a site build with an archive review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Publish [build directory] to BrewPage in namespace [namespace] with link-only access and no password. If archive approval is required, show the manifest and wait.

prompt_templates.title: Update a Saved Site
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: replace a site while preserving its publication settings.
prompt_templates.prompt: From the original workspace, update [exact saved reader link] with [replacement directory]. Keep the current access and expiry settings. Stop if target validation or archive approval fails.

output_examples.input: Publish approved Markdown as a link-only BrewPage page.
output: BrewPage confirmed the publication and returned a reader link.
The anonymous owner credential was saved in private state for this workspace.

output_examples.input: Publish a site archive that contains files requiring review.
output: The archive manifest lists the flagged files and includes a digest for approval.

output_examples.input: Check an earlier create attempt whose result is unknown.
output: A create attempt is pending in this workspace.
The result includes its operation identifier, request digest, and whether a protected recovery receipt is available.

best_practices: Confirm the source, namespace, intended audience, and password choice before a write.
Review the exact archive manifest and file contents before approving a digest. Keep credentials outside the publish input.
Use the original workspace and exact reader link for updates. Check local recovery before retrying an uncertain create.
anti_patterns: Treating skill activation, draft preparation, or inspection as permission to publish.
Assuming link-only access restricts readers or filename checks catch every secret.
Creating a replacement after an update fails without asking for separate authorization.

faq.question: Does installing the skill publish anything?
faq.answer: No. A publication or update requires an explicit request that identifies the content or exact target.

faq.question: Who can access a link-only page?
faq.answer: Anyone with the reader link can open it unless the publication is password protected. Link-only access does not mean private access.

faq.question: Where are anonymous owner credentials saved?
faq.answer: The runner stores them in a private slot for the resolved workspace. It checks that the state path is outside Git and reports storage status without displaying owner proof.

faq.question: What does an archive confirmation mean?
faq.answer: No upload has occurred. Review the listed files, then approve only the exact archive identified by its digest.

faq.question: Can this edition use a connected BrewPage account?
faq.answer: No. Use a BrewPage integration that supports connected ownership when you need account authority or private receipt delivery.

faq.question: What should I do after an uncertain create?
faq.answer: Check pending status in the original workspace and recover the protected receipt if available. Leave the attempt pending until you can verify the outcome.
